components.name: Payment confirmation dialog
components.description: Scoped Soft Outline payment hierarchy with six actual stages, wrapping ENS route and a native blurred backdrop. Illustrative names and amount below are preview data. The application opens this dialog modally, selects copy from real payment state, and yields to wallet prompts. Its payment type sizes do not redefine the global typography scale.

Your proof is ready and the backup export was requested. Confirm only after the encrypted file is saved.

What happens behind the scenes?
ENS names
Account names are verified before entry. Destinations are checked again before approval and sending.
Chainlink CRE
This draft uses local compilation. A Chainlink CRE result was not supplied.
Private proof
Your device creates the proof. The sender knows its payment list; private allocation amounts are not published as plain text on chain.
Network visibility
Your connected wallet pays the network fee. The submitting address and timing are public. Network providers can observe your connection.

components.name: ENS entry verification
components.description: ENS entry retains the existing light entry panel, labeled inset name field, raised verification action, explicit status and optional approval-wallet explanation. This organization example is synthetic. Successful fresh verification opens the workspace directly; unavailable checks and Payment ID recovery keep their own clear paths. Session-restoration behavior is outside this component documentation review.
components.html:
Link your organization.

Use a verified ENS name for your organization’s approval wallet. People can see who they are paying with.

Which wallet needs this name?

The dedicated wallet that approves organization payments. Your personal wallet may pay gas, but its name does not identify the organization.

ENS linking is required

Finish linking to continue.

Your ENS name and linked public records are public. Private payment keys stay on your device. Linking a name does not grant organization approval.

narrative.overview: NULL combines crisp Outline structure with the stronger neumorphic treatment approved by the user: pale gray material, charcoal type, raised surfaces, and inset controls. Financial information stays compact and legible, with generous gutters and clear next actions. Authentication, inbox, funds, dialogs, and settings share this light visual system. The current authority is soft-outline.css over the structural styles.css; docs/DESIGN_REFERENCE.md is historical.
keyCharacteristics: One pale material with a consistent upper-left light source.
Charcoal actions, clear field outlines, and readable semantic status labels.
Raised task panels and controls alongside flat financial tables.
The supplied six-blade aperture logo and restrained Inter typography.

rules.name: User-approved tactile depth
rules.body: The explicit Outline plus stronger Neumorphism direction is a deliberate exception to generic no-shadow defaults. Use shared raised and inset tokens with visible outlines and semantic states.

dos: Do extend Soft Outline across all routes and light Privy authentication.
Do preserve the six-blade currentColor logo and original black public/logo.svg.
Do preserve real balances, masking, recovery, visible focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use flat financial tables and the full-width treasury with ledger beside the balance on desktop.
donts: Don't restore the dark Mercury palette or cobalt pill actions.
Don't rely on shadows alone for focus, controls, or status.
Don't invent balances, history, or unsupported privacy claims.
Don't treat simulated-session visual checks as live authentication or transaction verification.
